QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_14

question.text: A start-up with no revenue can be valued using:

answer.text: Adapted DCF, relative valuation using surrogate operating metrics, qualitative score-card factors, or the VC method
No method exists for pre-revenue companies

explanation.text: The Logic: Start-ups, especially pre-revenue ones, are valued using adapted DCF, relative valuation with surrogate operating metrics, qualitative score-card attributes, or the VC method. These approaches accommodate the limited financial history of early-stage businesses. The Trap: Only using a P/E ratio, demanding precise DCF projections, or assuming no method exists each ignore the workbook's catalogue of techniques specifically adapted for start-up situations. Note: Based on NISM Series XIX-A workbook pages 246-250, which list adapted DCF, relative valuation/surrogate metrics, qualitative score-card factors, and the VC method as start-up valuation approaches.
